name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised no money
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Garcia is an incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 17 points, and she has raised nearly a million dollars while her opponent has raised nothing. Markets price her near certain to win, so the forecast stays at a wide Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any sign of outside Republican spending or a polling surprise could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by 17 points. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent with strong name recognition in the community. Her campaign has raised about $987,000 and holds roughly $201,000 on hand, with outside groups adding more than $560,000 in support on her behalf.

Republican Martha Fierro faces steep odds: she has reported no fundraising and no outside backing, leaving her little ability to compete in a district where the fundamentals already favor Democrats by a wide margin. Prediction markets put Garcia's chances near 97 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
